title: Paramagnetic phase of MnTe$_2$: complete one phonon Raman spectrum
authors: Taras Palasyuk, Dominik Kurzydłowski, Ashutosh S. Wadge, Rajmund Bacewicz, Madhavi H. Dalsaniya, Michał Wierzbicki, Daniel Jastrzebski, Andrzej Wiśniewski, Wojciech Szuszkiewicz, Igor Antoniazzi, Bruno Camargo, Maciej R. Molas, Adam Babiński, Krzysztof Zberecki, Cezariusz Jastrzebski
abstract: In this study we present a complete first-order Raman scattering spectrum of paramagnetic phase of MnTe$_2$- a material, where new type of spin texture induced by noncoplanar antiferromagnetic ordering below the Néel temperature ($T_N \approx 90$ K) gives rise to unconventional scenario of magnetism. Basic properties of all five phonon modes ($A_g$, $E_g$ and three $T_g$) predicted by the group theory have been successfully approached through polarization, excitation and temperature dependent measurements. In particular, the ever-missing phonon mode of $T_g$ symmetry has been unambiguously resolved in the room temperature Raman spectrum at approximately 107 cm$^{-1}$, just 1.5 cm$^{-1}$ higher in frequency compared to the $E_g$ mode. Density functional theory calculations reproduce the observed Raman-active phonon spectrum and support the assignment of all five first-order Raman modes, including the near-degeneracy of the $E_g$ and one of the $T_g$ vibrations. The calculations further reveal a dense manifold of low-energy antiferromagnetic spin configurations, separated from the ground state by only a few meV per formula unit. Furthermore, strong signals of inelastically scattered light from the paramagnetic (PM) phase of MnTe$_2$ were acquired with long wavelength excitations, i.e. 633 nm and 785 nm, revealing the $2A_g$ overtone at approx. 360 cm$^{-1}$. The enhanced absorption of the light in the near infrared range could be a putative reason behind the anomalous angular dependence of scattered intensity of the highest frequency $T_g$ phonon mode (183 cm$^{-1}$) measured in PM MnTe$_2$ with parallelly aligned polarizers. Finally, upon cooling just below the $T_N$, the measured properties of phonons remained basically unperturbed by the incipient long-range antiferromagnetic ordering.
summary: This work presents a comprehensive spectroscopic analysis of the paramagnetic phase of MnTe2, using Raman scattering to map out its phonon spectrum. By combining polarization-resolved experiments with DFT calculations, the authors unambiguously identify multiple phonon modes and demonstrate that the lattice dynamics are largely unperturbed by the onset of magnetic ordering. This provides a detailed picture of the material's vibrational properties in a strongly correlated magnetic environment.
main_problem: The study aims to present a complete first-order Raman spectrum of the paramagnetic phase of MnTe2 and resolve ambiguities regarding its phonon modes, while also investigating the interplay between lattice and spin excitations.
main_result: The authors successfully resolved a previously missing phonon mode and used DFT calculations to reproduce the spectrum, confirming the vibrational properties of the paramagnetic state.
method: The research combines extensive experimental measurements (polarization-resolved, temperature-dependent, excitation-dependent Raman spectroscopy) with theoretical predictions from Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations.
model_or_system: The physical system is MnTe2, a material exhibiting unconventional magnetism with noncoplanar antiferromagnetic ordering below the Néel temperature. The study focuses on the lattice dynamics (phonons) in the paramagnetic phase.
key_observables: Five predicted phonon modes (A_g, E_g, and three T_g), phonon frequencies, polarization-dependent scattering intensities, and the $2A_g$ overtone signal.
important_parameters: Néel temperature (T_N ≈ 90 K), excitation energies (1.58 eV to 2.54 eV), and temperature range (80 K to 343 K).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on DFT calculations (using PBE/PBEsol functionals) to model the electronic structure and phonon dispersion, and assumes that the observed spectral features can be assigned to specific symmetry modes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate polarization-resolved spectra, angular dependence plots comparing parallel and perpendicular polarizations, and comparisons of spectra taken with different excitation wavelengths.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by establishing the experimental necessity of resolving all five phonon modes, detailing the polarization and temperature measurements, supporting the findings with DFT calculations, and finally discussing the implications for spin-lattice coupling.
why_interesting: The detailed study of lattice vibrations (phonons) in a magnetically ordered material like MnTe2 provides insight into magnetostriction and spin-phonon coupling, which are crucial topics in strongly correlated electron systems.
